chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: Forty dollars pro rata and Cincinnati
summary: The Armstrong band learns the $40 weekly pay was pro rata and stops getting paid full wages in Cincinnati.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: This is the band that you'd organized in Chicago, and you had gone down to Texas --
We'd gone down to Texas to play. So okay, in our travels we wind up in -- well, I'm going to -- first I'm going to tell you what our salary was. We made $40.00 a week, and that was pro rata. So --
What do you mean by that?
WEll that means you divide seven into 40, and that's what you made a night.
You know what I mean? So if you didn't
work seven nights, say if you worked three nights, what is that, seven into 40, it's a little over $5.00 a night, right?

So anyway, when we got into Cincinnati, Ohio, see, we really didn't know nothing about this pro rata until we hit Cincinnati, Ohio, and when we were going to get paid Mike came to us, he said, "Well you know, now we only worked three days last week, so --." We said, "What?" So we were supposed to open at Castle Farms, that was a famous ballroom in Cincinnati --
-- and at this time the bus was terminating their service with us, and he was going to deadhead back to Chicago.
